4. Uniform generation of the code representation

The supplied-representation qualification can also be removed for this family. The algorithm below pays the arithmetic construction rather than assuming a tower or a chart oracle.

4.1 Fixed preprocessing

All local code parameters, fields, and arithmetic choices are fixed before the requested logical size is known.

The preprocessor performs the following finite computations.

- 
Arithmetic seed. Construct a totally real number field with the prescribed residue degrees, a totally definite quaternion algebra split at the walking places and ramified at a finite place, and a maximal order. These choices can be found by deterministic enumeration with exact tests. For example, real-root and irreducibility tests decide the field conditions; local algebra tests decide the quaternion conditions. A maximal order can be obtained by enumerating the finite set of overorders between an initial order and its trace-dual lattice.


- 
Local actions and coefficient tables. Compute the finite-field representations, endpoint maps, local charts, and local right inverses. Their dimensions are fixed constants.


- 
A finite arithmetic quotient. Generate a quotient of the product of trees by breadth-first traversal and exact orbit testing.


The important algorithmic point in step 3 is that orbit testing terminates on both answers. Conditions that an element take one represented vertex to another bound its denominators at the finitely many walking places. Integrality bounds the remaining denominators. Reduced norm one in a totally definite quaternion algebra bounds every archimedean coordinate. The candidates therefore lie in a finite, effectively bounded lattice region, which can be enumerated exactly.

Cocompactness guarantees that quotient traversal eventually closes. A fixed initial congruence level ensures freeness; finite local-ball tests then find a level with the required cubical incidences and complete upward stars.
